facts.statement: The genus Striatolamia was described by Glikman in 1964.
Striatolamia is classified as an extinct genus of sharks in the family Odontaspididae.
facts.quote: Striatolamia is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the family Odontaspididae.

facts.statement: Striatolamia lived from the Early Paleocene to the Late Miocene, between 61.7 and 10.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: These extinct sharks lived from the Early Paleocene to Late Miocene (61.7 to 10.3 Ma).

facts.statement: The name Striatolamia comes from the Latin words for 'striped' and 'shark,' referring to the striations on its teeth.
facts.quote: The Latin genus name Striatolamia refers to the striations on the surface of the teeth.

facts.statement: Other authors have previously assigned Striatolamia to the families Mitsukurinidae and Striatolamiidae.
facts.quote: This genus had been assigned to families Mitsukurinidae and Striatolamiidae by other authors.

facts.statement: Species of Striatolamia could grow to a length of about 350 centimeters.
facts.quote: Striatolamia species could reach a length of about 350 cm.

facts.statement: The front teeth of Striatolamia had elongated crowns with striations on the inner face and small side cusplets.
facts.quote: The anterior teeth have elongated crowns, with striations on the lingual face and small lateral cusplets.

facts.statement: The teeth of S. striata are generally smaller, ranging from 13 to 51 mm, compared to 19 to 38 mm for S. macrota.
facts.quote: Teeth of striata are generally smaller (13 to 51 mm) than macrota (19 to 38 mm).

facts.statement: Striatolamia sharks lived in waters with low salinity.
facts.quote: These sharks lived in waters with low salinity.

facts.statement: Fossil teeth and vertebrae of Striatolamia have been found worldwide.
facts.quote: Fossil teeth and calcified vertebrae of Striatolamia species have been found all over the world.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Striatolamia as Mitsukurinidae.
The time range for Striatolamia is recorded as Campanian to Messinian, from 83.6 to 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Messinian (83.6 to 5.333 million years ago)
